summary: After Belgium took the Congo from Leopold II in 1908 it kept forced labor and segregation; at independence in 1960 Belgian-backed secessions and CIA plotting led to the 1961 murder of Prime Minister Patrice Lumumba.

evidence.note: Belgian labor tax and whipping of uranium miners from the 1900s through the 1940s
Segregated Leopoldville, the evolue system and colonial schooling
1959 unrest pushes Belgium to grant independence in June 1960
Belgian-armed secessions of Katanga and South Kasai start a civil war
Eisenhower signals Lumumba should be eliminated; CIA sends a poison
Lumumba flown to Katanga and executed with Belgian officials present
Long segment on Allende, US corporate pressure and the 1973 coup in Chile
Generals' putsch in Algiers and alleged CIA role in plots against de Gaulle
Church Committee of 1975 and resulting CIA oversight closes the covered years

notes: Primary subject set to the Belgian Congo as a place since the title frames the story as the Congo's post-Leopold history; Lumumba gets the most airtime but is treated as a sympathetic secondary. The transcript dates the Algiers putsch to 1962; it was April 1961. Belgium's 2001 apology and 2018 square are a short coda, so reaches_present is false. Pinochet's rule to 1990 is a one-line mention.
